summary: The root ندم (ndm) primarily signifies grieving, regretting, or repenting for past actions. It can also imply disliking something.
lane: 1 نَدِمَ عَلَى مَا فَعَلَ ذ He grieved for what he had done; regretted it; repented of it: or he disliked it. (Msb.)

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: نَدِمَ عَلَى مَا فَعَلَ He grieved for what he had done; regretted it; repented of it: or he disliked it. (Msb.)
نَدِيمٌ A companion in drinking; a cup-companion. (S, Msb, K.) And hence, Any convivial companion; a boon-companion.
مَنْدَمٌ Repentance: an inf. n. of نَدِمَ; see an ex. in a verse of El-Kattál El-Kilábee, cited voce أَىٌّ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
